question: After successful exact-head live proof, should Crabbox ship GitHub Codespaces as a built-in direct provider that requires codespace-scoped authentication and deletes clean claim-owned Codespaces by default?
rationale: Tests can validate local invariants, but only maintainers can accept the permanent product, billing, credential-scope, and destructive-cleanup boundary for a new built-in provider.

options.title: Ship After Live Proof
options.body: Require the complete redacted lifecycle proof, then accept the documented direct-provider and delete-on-release contract if no residue or ownership failure appears.

options.title: Narrow Cleanup Defaults
options.body: Keep the provider but default release to stop-and-retain, making deletion an explicit trusted configuration choice with separate proof.

options.title: Pause Built-In Support
options.body: Do not merge the provider until maintainers want to own the Codespaces billing, authentication, and cleanup surface in core.

recommendation.title: Ship After Live Proof
recommendation.body: Require the complete redacted lifecycle proof, then accept the documented direct-provider and delete-on-release contract if no residue or ownership failure appears.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the explicit repository MEMBER in the supplied discussion and have repeatedly maintained the branch while enforcing the proof and risk gates.
